title: Spinach and Artichoke Dip
subtitle: Baked cream cheese and cheese dip with spinach and artichoke hearts
excerpt: Spinach and artichoke dip is a baked American party dip made from cream cheese, soured cream, mozzarella, and Parmesan with spinach and tinned artichoke hearts. It's hot, rich, and melted through, and disappears fast with bread or tortilla chips.
sourceNotes: Spinach and artichoke dip became a standard of American chain restaurant menus in the 1990s. The tinned artichoke + cream cheese base is the universal formula.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dip mixture ahead and refrigerate for up to two days. Bake from cold; add five minutes to the cooking time.

content.text: Spinach and artichoke dip is a baked American party snack: rich, bubbly, and designed to be eaten straight from the dish with bread or chips. The artichoke hearts give it body and a slight earthiness; the spinach adds bulk. Everything else is cheese and cream. It's one of the easiest party dishes to make, and reliably the first thing to disappear.
Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C / gas mark 5). Squeeze the thawed {{spinach-frozen}} in a clean tea towel or in handfuls until as much water as possible has been removed. Roughly chop.

Combine {{cream-cheese}}, {{soured-cream}}, {{plain-yoghurt}}, {{garlic}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, {{black-pepper}}, and {{chilli-flakes}} in a large bowl. Mix until smooth. Stir in the squeezed spinach, {{artichoke-hearts-tinned}}, half the {{mozzarella}}, and most of the {{parmesan}}.

Transfer to a baking dish. Scatter the remaining {{mozzarella}} and {{parmesan}} over the top. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the top is golden and the edges are bubbling. Leave to cool for five minutes before serving, it comes out very hot. Serve with sliced baguette, tortilla chips, or toasted pitta.

items.symptom: The dip is watery and thin
items.fix: This is the single most important step. Squeeze the thawed spinach in batches, hard, until no more liquid comes out. Frozen spinach holds an enormous amount of water.

items.symptom: The top browns too quickly before the centre is hot
items.cause: Dip spread too thin, or oven too hot.
items.fix: Use a deeper dish. The dip should be at least 3 cm deep. If the top is browning too fast, cover with foil for the last ten minutes.
Taste before baking and adjust: it should taste well-seasoned at room temperature before it goes in the oven. The cheese adds some salt but the dip needs more than you'd expect.

items.symptom: The artichoke hearts are too chunky and dominate
items.cause: Roughly chopped means different things to different people.
items.fix: Roughly chopped means about 2 cm pieces. Smaller lets them integrate with the spinach; larger gives a more chunky texture. Both are fine, adjust to preference.

content.text: Spinach and artichoke dip is one of those American chain restaurant dishes that became so widely repped in the 1990s it turned into a genre. The formula hasn't changed much because it works: warm cheese and cream, artichoke for texture, spinach for colour and substance. It's a reliably good party dish that can be made completely ahead and baked just before guests arrive.
